title: Tissue-aware priors transfer integration from blood to solid organs
abstract: Integration methods tuned on blood lose retention on solid organs. A tissue-aware prior on the batch factor restores it without retraining, and its strength can be set without cell-type labels.

fulltext_excerpt: Most integration methods were tuned on blood. Solid organs differ. Integration methods tuned on blood lose up to thirty percent of cell-type retention when applied to kidney and liver atlases. Epithelial gradients were the populations most often collapsed. We add a prior on the batch factor whose shape depends on the tissue. A tissue-aware prior on the batch factor restores retention on solid tissue without retraining the integration model. The prior changes only the inference step, so existing trained models can be reused. The prior strength can be chosen from the batch-to-biology variance ratio without any cell-type labels. This avoids the circularity of tuning against the labels one is later scored on. Our benchmark remains restricted to one well-annotated tissue per organ, so cross-organ generalisation is not established.
